headline: Rising rates hit bonds and credit, and the balanced mix lost {port_abs} in September
takeaway_fact: The hypothetical portfolio returned {port} against {bench} for the benchmark, a difference of {active}. The bond sleeve returned {fi_sleeve} and subtracted {fi_contrib_abs}, about {fi_share} of the decline. The equity sleeve returned {eq_sleeve}: US and emerging-market gains offset losses in Canada. [prices]
takeaway_view: Canadian stocks and bonds both fell, so the domestic cushion was missing. Holdings outside Canada, and a weaker Canadian dollar, kept the loss small.
overview_note: Total and price returns of ETF proxies, CAD. Yields and USD/CAD: Bank of Canada, latest value {macro_asof} (Sep 30 was a federal holiday). [prices][boc_valet]
theme_title: Theme: rates repriced higher and bonds paid for it
theme_evidence: The Federal Reserve raised its target range by 1/4 point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent on September 16, in a 12 to 0 vote. [fed_2026_09_16]
On September 2 the Bank of Canada held at {policy}%, saying financial conditions had tightened since July and long-term yields had moved up globally, including in Canada. [boc_2026_09_02]
Canada's 2-year yield rose {y2_chg} to {y2_1}% and the 10-year {y10_chg} to {y10_1}% (latest {macro_asof}). In CAD, XBB returned {ret_XBB}, XSB {ret_XSB} and XHY {ret_XHY}. [boc_valet][prices]
theme_view: Rising yields lower the price of existing bonds. The broad index fell more than the short-term fund and the lowest-quality bonds fell most, which fits that mechanism. XIC fell too ({ret_XIC}), so the Canadian stock-bond pair gave no offset, while XUU returned {ret_XUU} as USD/CAD rose {fx_chg}. The sources describe these moves but do not isolate causes.
equity_view: US ({ret_XUU}) and emerging markets ({ret_XEC}) rose; Canada ({ret_XIC}) and developed international ({ret_XEF}) fell. The sleeve ended at {eq_end_w} of the portfolio, {eq_drift} above target.
fi_view: The sleeve returned {fi_sleeve} and subtracted {fi_contrib_abs}. Shorter maturities held up better, consistent with lower rate sensitivity. [prices]
rebalance: Maintain. The largest holding drift is {max_hold_drift} (band {hold_band}); the largest sleeve drift is {max_class_drift} (band {class_band}). No trade triggers, so drifted weights carry into October. A reset would trade {turnover} of the portfolio.
counter: For acting: the Federal Reserve is tightening; moving part of XBB into XSB would lower rate sensitivity. For patience: drift is inside the bands, and selling bonds after a decline locks in the loss without evidence of where yields go next.
risks: Rates: the Bank of Canada sees higher upside risk to inflation. [boc_2026_09_02]
Trade: new US tariffs and Canadian counter-measures. [boc_2026_09_02]
Credit: XHY fell {ret_XHY}; a currency reversal would trim foreign equity.
monitor: Bank of Canada and MPR, Oct 28
methodology: Total return: closing prices, distributions reinvested at the ex-date close, net of fund expenses. Beginning weights are August's drifted weights (decision: Maintain). Contribution is weight times return, not formal attribution. Foreign-market ETFs are CAD-listed, so no currency conversion is applied.

notes: Main message. In September 2026 the hypothetical 60/40 portfolio returned {port} in Canadian dollars and the benchmark returned {bench}. Bonds subtracted {fi_contrib_abs}, about {fi_share} of the decline, while equities were roughly flat because US and emerging-market gains offset losses in Canada and developed international markets. The theme is rates: the Fed raised its range to 3-3/4 to 4 percent on September 16 and Canada's 2-year yield rose {y2_chg}. Bank of Canada series end on {macro_asof} because September 30 was a federal holiday. For a client: higher yields pushed bond prices down, and Canadian stocks fell as well.

Portfolio implications. The equity sleeve was flat but dispersion was wide. The bond sleeve fell {fi_sleeve}, and the short-term fund held up better than the broad index. The illustrative rule says maintain: the largest drift is {max_hold_drift}, inside the {hold_band} band, and a reset would trade {turnover} of the portfolio. Weights this month began from August's drifted weights because August's decision was Maintain. This illustrates a rule, not advice for any client.

Risks and monitoring. More yield increases would extend bond losses; the Bank of Canada says upside inflation risks increased and tariffs add uncertainty to growth. XHY fell {ret_XHY}, a reminder that credit can weaken with equities. Next events: the Bank of Canada decision and Monetary Policy Report on October 28 and the FOMC meeting on October 27 and 28. The counterargument is to shorten bond duration now; the case for patience is that drift is small and selling after a decline locks in the loss.
